title: Finite Q3 inverse-free sandwiched Schatten-Hoelder commutator envelope
question: Can a symmetric rho^(1/4)-sandwiched state norm bound a Q3 cutoff commutator by four-leg Schatten-4 factors without inverse Gibbs powers, and do the finite rows provide a uniform local fourth-moment estimate?

mathematical_interface.state: rho is a finite-dimensional positive Gibbs density matrix and S=rho^(1/4).
mathematical_interface.reason: Write S[W,A]S=(SW)(AS)-(SA)(WS), apply Schatten Holder to each product, then use the triangle inequality.
mathematical_interface.domain_advantage: Only positive quarter powers of the finite Gibbs state are used; no rho^(-1/2), modular inverse, or finite support floor is used in the inequality.

lean_crosscheck.role: R346 checks the exact nonnegative two-leg scalar assembly used by the finite Schatten-Hoelder envelope; matrix Schatten calculus and all limits remain Python evidence.

adversarial_review.check: The factorization keeps S on the displayed side of each factor and never commutes rho, W, or A.
Each product uses 1/2=1/4+1/4, and the finite code computes singular-value p=4 norms rather than an entrywise surrogate.
Both W A-A W and its adjoint history are evaluated; reversing the sign cannot improve the declared two-sided bound.
The new norm uses only rho^(1/4); no inverse power is formed. Full-rank probabilities are reported only as finite Gibbs construction diagnostics.
Source and disjoint-tail commutators are measured for every finite volume and cutoff instead of inferred from labels.
The finite four-leg factors are summarized across beta, volume, radius, time, interpolation and both orientations; finite maxima are not called a common-core bound.
Oscillator dimensions are explicit and no finite matrix inequality is promoted to the unbounded CCR domain.
The independent lane reconstructs the oscillator, graph, Q3 Hamiltonian, cutoff, Gibbs quarter root, histories and singular-value norms without importing the primary lane.
R346 certifies only scalar nonnegative assembly and an exact rational fixture, not Schatten Holder, spectral calculus, or QFT limits.
No direct D/delta-D Cauchy theorem, modular-domain transfer, common OS carrier, exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure is inferred.
